anomalies.observed: In the 'Water Level Sensor / Safety Switches' block the two float-switch pull resistors are drawn as R6 = 10 kΩ on the FLOAT_HIGH side and R9 = 4.7 kΩ on the FLOAT_LOW side, both returned toward +3V3.
anomalies.expected: The specification's netlist data has the values and nets the other way round: R6 = 10 kΩ pulling FLOAT_LOW to +3V3, and R9 = 10 kΩ pulling FLOAT_HIGH to GND.

evidence.quote: with 10 kΩ/4.7 kΩ pull resistors visible in the .cir file: R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k, R2 FLOAT_LOW /BPUMP 4.7k, R11 FLOAT_HIGH /BATO 4.7k
Safety Switches: R6 10k / C5 100n on the FLOAT_HIGH line, R9 4k7 / C4 100n on the FLOAT_LOW line

anomalies.impact: The low-water and high-water float inputs would be biased to the wrong default level / the R9 pull is the wrong strength, so the low-level pump cutoff and the high-level overflow interlock can fail to assert (or assert inverted), defeating the ATO safety interlocks.

anomalies.observed: The 'Environmental Sensor (optional)' header H6 (for the BME280) is drawn fed from the +5V rail, while the neighbouring light-sensor header H5 uses +3V3.
anomalies.expected: The specification states both I2C sensor headers break out the 3.3 V rail: 'H5, H6 (4-pin JST-PH headers) — each breaks out +3V3, GND, I2C_SCL, I2C_SDA'.

evidence.quote: H5, H6 (4-pin JST-PH headers) — each breaks out +3V3, GND, I2C_SCL, I2C_SDA

anomalies.impact: A 3.3 V-only BME280 (and its I2C levels) would be over-driven from the 5 V rail, risking damage or non-compliant bus levels instead of the intended 3.3 V interface.

parsed.summary: The build does not fully match the intended design: the two float-switch pull resistors (R6/R9) are on the opposite float nets and R9 is 4.7 kΩ instead of the specified 10 kΩ, and (less certainly) the environmental-sensor header H6 is powered from +5V rather than the specified +3V3. Both would change behaviour of the water-level sensing/protection circuitry.
